## 固定收益市場主論點

9月28日美國公債再度下跌，短天期券吐回上週五的反彈。荷莫茲海峽協議未能取得進展，能源價格居高不下，投資人預期聯準會將進一步升息。彭博盤末報導指出，10年期殖利率上升9個基點至5.25%，盤中一度觸及5.27%的19年高點。沙烏地阿拉伯管線輸油恢復，雖使稍早油價急漲的幅度收斂，布蘭特原油在固定收益交易時段結束時仍收在每桶$105.28，上漲0.92%。

壓力已從基準利率擴及借款人的融資條件。美國投資級、高收益及新興市場硬通貨債券利差明顯擴大。Paramount以最高約9%的非投資級債券殖利率，為收購融資吸引大量初步需求；市政債發行人及印度國營企業則延後或縮減發行。聯準會理事Lisa Cook進一步質疑人工智慧能否在短期內緩解通膨：相關投資已開始爭奪電力與營建人力，生產力效益卻要更晚才會出現。歐洲央行總裁拉加德則更重視債券殖利率上升已帶來的抑制效果，使市場對ECB立即升息的預期降溫。

## 能源衝擊再起，實質殖利率同步攀升

上週五支撐短天期公債回升的樂觀情緒消退，美國公債週一再遭賣壓。美國總統川普拒絕伊朗提出、為期7天的荷莫茲海峽重啟方案，德黑蘭也維持原有條件。美國交易時段傳出，華府可能以制裁鬆綁換取核議題進展，帶動油價與股市脫離當日最差水準，但公債殖利率直到午後尾盤仍保留大部分漲幅。川普其後否認曾提出制裁鬆綁，外交途徑仍不明朗。

實體供給帶來較具體的緩衝。沙烏地阿拉伯東西向輸油管線先前遭無人機攻擊損壞，據報無人機由伊拉克境內發動。管線修復後恢復出口，輸送量達每日約350萬桶，約為管線運能的一半。沙國同時利用荷莫茲海峽及西側路線，將整體出口提高至每日逾500萬桶的戰時高點，多數運往亞洲。供給改善使油價漲幅收斂，但海峽通航尚未恢復正常。

替代路線仍受到紅海及曼德海峽周邊胡塞武裝的威脅。歐盟外交與安全政策高級代表Kaja Kallas週一表示，已有兩國表達可能為「盾牌行動」（Operation Aspides）增派船艦的意願。商船等待護航，但任務現有船艦不足，主要僅有3艘義大利及希臘軍艦，遠低於最初評估至少需要的10艘。Kallas提議調用原已承諾投入另一項擬議荷莫茲海峽任務、但尚未部署的船艦；各國表達增援意願，尚未轉為實際部署。

彭博每日殖利率序列的9月28日數值顯示，美國2年期公債殖利率上升7.8個基點至4.932%，5年期上升8.3個基點至5.071%；10年期上升7.4個基點至5.237%，30年期上升5.4個基點至5.548%。2年與10年期利差僅收窄0.4個基點至30.5個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄2.4個基點至61.6個基點。與上週五各期限表現分歧不同，這次短中天期券也全面加入跌勢。

10年期實質殖利率上升7個基點至2.894%，損益兩平通膨率僅增加0.4個基點至2.343%。當日名目殖利率升幅絕大部分來自實質借貸成本，而非長期通膨補償同步大幅攀升，符合市場預期聯準會將回應持續物價壓力的情境。這也說明，油價再度居高的交易日，為何對不提供利息收益的資產格外不利：黃金期貨下跌3.54%至每盎司$4,168.40，美元指數上漲0.23%至101.20。

Cook週一談話指出AI通膨辯論的關鍵在於時間落差。她預期，生產力提升將在未來幾年帶來溫和的通膨降溫效果，但來不及抵銷2026年稍晚更廣泛的通膨壓力。過去一年電力與用水成本已上漲約5%，資料中心投資又加劇能源及營建人力的競爭。企業承諾投入的$2兆資本，目前只支出一小部分；AI相關股票上漲，也在支撐消費。

她支持9月升息，認為這是處理高通膨的必要措施，後續決策則取決於經濟數據。她判斷勞動市場大致平衡且逐步改善，失業率下降、整體經濟具韌性，足以承受較高利率。她仍不確定AI多快能提升全體經濟生產力，但並未否定其最終效益。週一報導期間，聯邦資金期貨反映10月再次升息的機率約70%；交換市場已完全反映未來一年至少升息3次、每次25個基點，並保留第4次升息的可能。

當日達拉斯聯準銀行製造業指數呈現另一項幅度較溫和的景氣訊號：9月由11.6降至9.8，但遠高於預估的1。依此指標，製造業雖然放緩，卻未接近經濟學家原先預期的疲弱程度。它沒有重現上週全國企業調查的加速情形，也不支持工廠活動即將急遽萎縮的看法。

高物價終將損及需求的風險，使債券投資人看法分歧。Wellington的Brij Khurana認為，大宗商品價格長期高企會侵蝕實質所得、破壞需求，而市場逐一追逐外交新聞交易，反而忽略了這項風險。Columbia Threadneedle的Ed Al-Hussainy預期，隨緊縮政策壓低經濟活動，2年與10年、5年與30年期曲線將在六個月內倒掛。道明證券Gennadiy Goldberg的短期看法相反：市場已反映相當幅度的升息，短端更難持續落後，曲線較可能走陡。週一仍為正值的2年與10年期利差，尚不足以判定哪方看法正確。

Jim Bianco則六年來首次轉為看好美國公債。他將旗下WisdomTree基金所追蹤指數的存續期間提高至逾6年，高於彭博美國綜合債券指數的5.7年，但強調是逐步調整，而非積極押注。彭博的報酬試算顯示，以目前價格計算，10年期殖利率須在一年內升至接近6%，才會耗盡利息收益的緩衝；殖利率上升1個百分點所對應的損失不到2%，同幅度下降則可帶來約13%的獲利。這些是前瞻報酬情境，並不能防止短期再遭拋售。Bianco認為目前附近的殖利率在歷史上屬正常水準，並非迫近危機的訊號。

即使估值論點浮現，避險需求仍持續增加。iShares 20年以上美國公債ETF的選擇權20日平均成交量創新高；未平倉量較一年前增加逾一倍，逼近前一週到期日前所創的1,355萬口高點。隱含波動率與偏空賣權的溢價均升至3月底以來最高。野村Alex Kosoglyadov表示，傳統股票投資人除股票波動率工具外，也愈來愈常使用利率商品。標普500週一下跌0.77%，那斯達克100下跌1.08%，融資成本調整對股市的影響更為明顯。

紐約聯準銀行週一公布的研究，則提供美國公債市場融資結構的長期背景。Gara Afonso、Jin-Wook Choi、Gonzalo Cisternas與Ryan Riordan指出，美國附買回市場規模約$13.5兆，相當於GDP的40%，其中約70%以美國公債擔保。避險基金借款由2013年的$4,000億增至2023年的$1.5兆，再升至2025年底的$3兆；貨幣市場基金放款在2026年1月達$3兆，五年前則為$1兆。避險基金在2025年底也提供約$1.3兆放款，用途包括流動性管理及擔保品轉換。這段歷史擴張顯示支撐證券部位的融資規模，並非週一資金流量的衡量。

## Paramount試探買盤，其他發行人選擇等待

Paramount Skydance的收購融資，已從市場預期的供給負擔，進展到可觀察的投資人需求，但仍待最終定價。週一上午，規模約等值$124億的非投資級債券已吸引逾$230億訂單；尚未啟動發行、規模約$320億的較高評級債券，也獲投資人表達逾$510億的認購意向。這兩部分債券加上$75億貸款，構成收購Warner Bros. Discovery所需$520億融資方案的大部分。

發行人提供的報酬相當可觀。10年期美元第二順位擔保債券初步討論的殖利率約9%，彭博指數中同評級流通債券平均則為6.9%；5年期歐元非投資級券的報價約7.5%。較高評級部分擬發行8批美元第一順位擔保債，期限介於2至40年；第二順位擔保部分則包括5年與8年期歐元券，以及5年、8年與10年期美元券。投資人看到最終條款後，初步認購意向仍可能改變。

第一順位債的評級分歧，反映各機構對優先融資所依賴假設的不同判斷。惠譽及標普給予投資級評等，穆迪則評為低於投資級1級；三家均將第二順位債列為非投資級。穆迪指出，收購將增加逾$300億債務，使槓桿接近盈餘的7倍，並提到股權集中、擬新增順位高於既有無擔保債權人的債權，以及管理階層達成財務目標的紀錄好壞參半。標普的BBB-評等，則較看重Ellison家族承諾在2028年將槓桿降至3.75倍、2029年降至3倍。

依融資架構，延誤成本由Paramount而非承銷銀行承擔。公司力求在週三前完成債券與貸款定價；若無法在10月之前完成這筆$1,100億收購，就須每天向Warner股東支付$700萬。因此，大額訂單與推介新券時提出的高殖利率並存，同時反映投資人的承接能力，以及借款人難以等待的處境。

高盛Amanda Lynam週一表示，繼夏季稍早投資級市場出現類似情況後，大量高收益債供給也開始考驗投資人吸收新券的能力。截至上週五，9月非投資級債發行達$385.1億，為2026年最繁忙月份。她估計今年各債務市場與AI相關的借款接近$6,000億，其中僅約40%來自超大規模雲端業者。這波融資涵蓋範圍廣泛，避開少數熟悉的科技公司，並不代表避開了相關曝險。

銀行洽談Paramount發債時，部分次級市場債券已重新定價。據報導援引的Trace成交觀察，SpaceX票息5.65%、2033年到期債券的利差擴大約36個基點至基準以上177個基點；Oracle票息2.95%、2030年到期債券則擴大約15個基點至160個基點。Allspring交易員Mark Clegg認為，Paramount龐大的發行規模正迫使投資人重新評估整體市場的利差補償。若順利配售，也可能鼓勵原本等待市場接受度趨穩的借款人進場。

另有新報導說明，SoftBank已完成的發行如何取得美國機構資金。法律安排的核心，是避免依《投資公司法》被歸類為投資公司，以免增加外國發行人進入市場的難度。SoftBank表示，投資證券占其未合併資產不到40%，並將持有86%股權的Arm視為營運子公司，而非被動投資。這項架構協助其依Rule 144A發債；報導揭露的是接觸這批投資人的安排，並非另一筆新增融資。

其他市場的發行人則選擇等待。洛杉磯會展中心$18億債券發行改為視每日市況決定，原訂9月24日的納許維爾會展中心約$7.77億交易也採相同安排；紐澤西運輸信託基金管理局約$17億發行同樣暫緩。紐約時間週一下午2時，30年期市政債基準殖利率達5.18%，為至少2011年1月以來最高，當月累計上升約60個基點，直接壓縮借新還舊可節省的成本。摩根大通策略師預期，若市況持續，每週實際發行可能比公布的供給預估少$10億至$30億。

印度借款人面臨類似的價格限制，國內流動性收縮又加重壓力。Sagarmala Finance週一取消最高INR60億的藍色債券計畫，因為10年期券投標票息高於其低於8%的預期。Power Grid雖在7.74%收到足額投標，仍僅接受原計畫INR500億中的INR200億。SIDBI上週五在投標利率介於7.6%至8.1%後，取消INR600億、2029年12月到期債券；該機構9月稍早發行2029年10月到期債的利率為7.70%。印度央行回收資金，銀行體系剩餘流動性由月初近INR11兆降至INR4.6兆，在全球殖利率上升之外，再添一股國內緊縮力量。

平價健身房連鎖PureGym的再融資情況形成對照。公司正向投資人推介£14億、6年期優先擔保債，歐元券殖利率約6.5%、英鎊券約8%，低於2023年所發債券逾8%的殖利率。惠譽因營運改善、新店開設及美國業務轉強，將發行人評等由B-上調至B。募集資金將償還既有債券，並部分償還特別股融資，但槓桿會暫時上升。預計截至2029年將新增近300家健身房，擴張支出將使自由現金流持續為負，限制營業獲利改善帶來的好處。

巴西肉品加工商MBRF也開始與投資人通話，研議Marfrig收購BRF後的首次發債。選項包括期限略長於7年、前3年不可贖回的債券，或略長於10年、前5年不可贖回的債券。標普與惠譽給予擬發行債券BB+評等。另有一項買回$4.675億、2029年到期債券的要約，將於10月2日截止。新融資尚未公布最終規模或殖利率。

## 央行評估市場升息已帶來多少緊縮

拉加德週一向歐洲議員表示，全球殖利率上升將使歐元區成長放緩，並抑制能源成本向物價轉嫁，效果可能強於ECB在9月所預估。由於尚未出現第二輪通膨效應，她傾向審慎因應。交易員因此下修升息預期，10月升息機率降至40%以下。

她並未否定通膨持續的風險。ECB必須預判第二輪效應，而非等其成形才行動，但目前尚未看到這類效應可能出現的證據。她稱現行利率位於2%至2.5%中性區間的上緣，同時強調政策不會機械式依此估計決定。她也批評涵蓋過廣或沒有終止期限的能源補助，主張措施應暫時且具針對性；否則，市場利率開始抑制支出時，財政措施反而可能繼續支撐需求。

英國央行副總裁Dave Ramsden週一也表達有條件支持升息。若通膨上行壓力持續累積，他將考慮升息，重點觀察國內食品價格的第二輪效應，以及雇主即將提出的薪資協商計畫。不過，他仍認為現行政策已具限制性：若沒有戰爭，他原本預期至今至少降息兩次，因此自3月以來維持利率，已比原先展望帶來更多緊縮。外部委員Swati Dhingra另警告，利率升高可能削弱投資與經濟供給能力。Ramsden立場轉變，使討論不再限於上週發言的官員，但對行動代價的分歧仍在。

英國財政政策也面臨相同的融資成本壓力。財政大臣John Healey週一承諾，他與首相Andy Burnham將遵守財政規則，並在10月28日預算案前，以產業成長計畫搭配支出紀律。他承諾投入£60億於造船廠，包括核嚇阻相關項目，另宣布地方學徒計畫，並釋出壓抑社福支出的訊號。2年期英國公債殖利率一度上升9個基點至4.93%，隨後因能源價格回落而吐回部分升幅。

政府相對主要預算規則的財政餘裕，估計已由春季接手時的£236億縮減約一半。CG Asset Management的Emma Moriarty認為，投資人將明確區分財政餘裕重建至接近£200億，或僅維持在約£100億的兩種情況。新推出的首購族股權貸款計畫，則使主要住宅建商股價上漲逾10%。在財政大臣籌備預計增稅、削減其他支出的預算案之際，該計畫先對住宅產業帶來即時刺激。

美國收盤後，智庫Common Wealth提議修改公營事業的會計處理，讓GB Energy及National Wealth Fund等機構以專案收益支持發債，且不計入全國財政總額。該智庫估計，類似處理使法國帳列債務占GDP比率降低2.8個百分點，德國則降低10.7個百分點。這項提案將改變投資資金由誰籌措及如何入帳，但尚非英國已採行的財政規則鬆綁。

日本的調整集中在短期利率預期。2年期公債殖利率最多上升4個基點至1.975%，創1995年以來最高；5年期上升3個基點至2.43%。週一隔夜利率交換反映日本央行10月升息機率約40%，並完全反映12月前再升息25個基點。前日本央行理事門間一夫認為，連續第二個月升息是可能的，終點利率或於2027年6月或7月達約2%，高於受訪經濟學家1.75%的中位數預估。他認為近期反對票未必阻止政策正常化，尤其阻撓正常化可能再次引發日圓貶值及輸入性通膨。

南韓在週四、週五假期後恢復交易，3年期殖利率跳升11個基點至4.11%，創2022年11月以來最高。NH Investment & Securities的Kang Seungwon表示，若聯準會10月再升息，很可能使南韓11月升息的預期更為確定。韓國央行週一召開市場檢視會議，承諾密切監測可能擴大的波動。市場重新開盤時，外部利率壓力與國內疑慮交疊：半導體帶動的強勁成長及輸入性能源通膨，可能需要更多緊縮。

Pimco則質疑澳洲還能升息多少。澳洲投資組合管理主管Adam Bowe週一表示，升息已充分反映在價格中，並看好5至10年期債券的機會。交換市場給予明年再升息兩次、使政策利率超過5%的情境75%機率，但Bowe指出，家庭稅負及房貸支出相對所得已接近歷史高點。資料中心投資可能支撐未來幾年的活動，負債消費者卻遠較難承受這條利率路徑。

摩根大通Charnon Boonnuch對泰國提出罕見偏鷹預測：自2027年第1季起升息3次、每次25個基點，使政策利率由1%升至1.75%，相較之下市場共識是直到明年底都不變。摩根大通維持2026與2027年成長預測均為2.5%，高於央行的2.3%與1.8%；並將2027年通膨預測上修1個百分點至2.5%，預期第1季通膨接近4%。不過，小企業放款疲弱、經濟活動低於潛能，仍使該行預測2026年剩餘時間維持利率不變。

中國長債的情境則不同。花旗Wenhan Chen與Rohit Garg預期，國內需求及信用創造偏弱將支撐長天期公債；其30年期公債交易建議的進場殖利率為2.088%，目標為1.80%。原計畫CNY1.3兆超長期特別國債已發行約90%，餘額可能在10月完成。他們也預期CNY3,600億金融機構增資將支撐長天期需求。8月工業利潤年增僅4.2%，為去年11月下滑以來最弱增速，凸顯復甦涵蓋範圍有限。

新公布細節的美中關稅安排，則在有限範圍內降低貿易摩擦：雙方各約$300億進口商品適用，去年雙邊商品貿易總額為$4,150億。美方清單有77項，中方涵蓋1,619項可能進口商品。北京另承諾2027與2028年各購買至少1,000萬公噸美國煤炭。減免集中於非敏感商品，出口管制及台灣議題仍未解決。

## 信用損失取決於現金流與債權順位

Merlin Entertainments說明，解決到期債務不一定改善既有債權人的處境。其€7億、2030年6月到期債券週一約報面額的69.3%，較9月10日宣布£6.57億融資前下跌約12個百分點。新貸款將取代明年到期的$8.3億無擔保債券，但順位與其他£32億債務並列，並對包括倫敦眼在內的高價值英國景點取得額外優先債權。

以有擔保融資取代無擔保債權，削弱了既有優先債權人之下可吸收損失的保護層。標普將擔保債B-評等列入負向信用觀察，穆迪則將貸款降至Caa2。Merlin上半年消耗£2,500萬現金。標普指出，一項資產出售應可使流動性對未來一年資金需求的覆蓋率提高至1.5倍以上，但2029年仍有$25億定期貸款到期。Polen Capital的Ben Pakenham認為，要讓債券回到面額，必須有顯著盈餘復甦或股本挹注，僅緩解到期壓力並不足夠。

即使美國整體消費仍有韌性，休閒產業借款人已出現壓力。Dave & Buster's獲利疲弱，穆迪週一將其展望改為負向；2031年到期貸款指示價格為面額的61.8%，較月初下跌逾15個百分點。Lucky Strike的2032年貸款約報79%，一個月下跌5個百分點；此前標普因營運轉弱及收購相關槓桿，將評等由B降至B-。公司管理階層將同店營收下降歸因於電視體育賽事吸走顧客。

但也有重要例外。AMC在疫情以來最強的一季後，完成約$40億融資。Michaels因銷售改善及減債，週一獲標普由B-升至B，第一及第二順位擔保債評等分別升至B與CCC+。兩種債券均在面額的98%附近交易，即使升評，仍較前一週低約1個百分點。標普仍指出，Apollo持有期間槓桿可能再升，加上消費支出轉弱、依賴中國進口，以及運輸受關稅與燃料成本影響，均構成風險。

澳洲Metrics Credit Partners揭露，旗下3檔上市基金合計減記約A$1.69億，並在9月30日會計截止日前暫停交易。Real Estate Multi-Strategy Fund減記約A$4,700萬至A$3.37億；Income Opportunities Trust減記A$7,300萬至A$6.43億；Master Income Trust減記A$4,900萬至A$24億。該管理機構管理約A$400億資產。澳洲證券投資委員會ASIC在更廣泛的私募信貸檢視中，已調查估值及治理疑慮，但未指控Metrics違規。這次是監管檢視下具體的帳面價值調降，不只是對產業再次表達疑慮。

Optimum債權人週一在紐約提告，使重整爭議升高至訴訟。他們要求撤銷若干交易，指控交易將擔保品及價值移轉給控股股東Patrick Drahi與其他內部人士。核心爭議之一是5月透過不受限制子公司發行的特別股：債權人指控，若貸款人執行權利，該架構會增加特別股持有人可取得的款項，使執行債權相較協議解決更為不利。Optimum否認不當行為，稱所有行動均符合債務契約及法律。逾$260億債務的協商仍在進行，對象也包括參與訴訟的債權人。

OTP Bank評估退出俄羅斯，則面臨另一種資產負債表取捨。執行長Peter Csanyi表示，銀行透過Luminor擴張波羅的海業務之際，預計年底前完成退出評估。OTP稱，俄國退出規則使賣方只能取得資產市值約5%的款項，目前幾乎不可能出售。銀行已匯回約$8.8億股息，但表示這些資金未用於收購Luminor。愛沙尼亞監管機關將俄國業務列為收購審查的關鍵問題。彭博取得的文件並未證實有違反制裁行為，OTP也稱內部審查未發現不合規情事；其股價週一仍一度下跌3.8%。

## 新興市場債務遭遇各國個別逆風

美國公債殖利率攀升與利差擴大，抹去新興市場美元債2026年所剩漲幅。彭博新興市場硬通貨綜合指數9月下跌約2.1%，對利率更敏感的主權債總報酬指標則下跌約2.4%。貝萊德規模$130億的EMB基金前一週流出$6.1億，為3月以來最大單週贖回；週一經配息調整後報酬為負0.91%。

經理人同時調整信用品質及利率曝險。Aegon的Jeff Grills減碼哥倫比亞，增持印尼、沙烏地阿拉伯及菲律賓；Neuberger Berman的Gorky Urquieta減碼厄瓜多、多明尼加共和國與尚比亞。摩根資產管理Pierre-Yves Bareau降低組合對信用市場拋售的敏感度，並將部分風險移向當地市場，包括他認為交換利率定價過度偏鷹的墨西哥。硬通貨債利差仍接近長期低點，意味著即使再融資需求尚未增加，投資人對各國突發衝擊所獲補償已有限。

厄瓜多週一就出現此類衝擊。總統Daniel Noboa出人意料撤換財政部長Sariha Moya，由原國家社會安全機構主席Bernardo Cordovez接任；該機構是國內債券的重要投資人。2039年美元債價格下跌2.3個百分點至面額的92.9%。Noboa前一週才說Moya將赴紐約會晤投資人。StoneX的Ramiro Blazquez表示，在財政不確定性及聖嬰現象威脅之下，這次未說明原因的人事更動令人不安。

Cordovez接手時，燃料補貼成本正上升，本地石油產量下降，煉油能力不足以滿足需求。洪災威脅沿海基礎建設及蝦、香蕉出口，高地乾旱則可能干擾水力發電；11月地方選舉進一步增加控制支出的難度。巴克萊Jason Keene已在前一週因補貼及天候風險下調投資建議，厄瓜多債券9月下跌4.5%。部長更換並未解決這些壓力，反而增添不確定性。

哥倫比亞總統Abelardo de la Espriella週日晚間表示，已指示經濟團隊因應財政危機，與IMF展開磋商，之後哥倫比亞披索下跌1.5%。墨西哥披索下跌1.7%，逼近每美元18披索，為3月底以來最弱。富國銀行Alvaro Vivanco認為，墨西哥走勢部分來自市場熱門的披索多頭及收取固定利率部位調整。匯率貶值正成為美國市場重新定價影響各國通膨與政策選擇的另一條途徑。

彭博對智利的調查顯示，19位分析師及交易員中有11位預期，聯準會將主導10月市場方向。儘管7月經濟活動較6月萎縮1.7%，2030年到期披索債殖利率仍升至5.74%，9月累計上升逾25個基點。1年期損益兩平通膨率當月增加56個基點至3.87%，2年期增加約37個基點至3.49%。市場將智利升息25個基點的預期時點，由9月稍早的至少一年後，提前至六個月內；但受訪者除1人外，均預期10月會議維持利率4.5%。這種分歧反映近期匯率與能源壓力，正與疲弱的國內景氣相互拉扯。

印尼一筆政府保證債權則獲得有利解決。Waskita Karya未按期還款後，政府及PT Penjaminan Infrastruktur Indonesia全額支付IDR7,220億本金求償，其中政府提供IDR6,100億，PII提供IDR1,120億，預定週一分配給債券持有人。這是疫情期間保證計畫首次賠付，完成時間遠早於20個營業日的期限，解決了這筆近期求償。官員強調，這筆款項既不是向Waskita提供新融資，也未免除該建商的償債義務。

辛巴威則逆著普遍緊縮方向，週一將基準利率由30%降至27.5%，連續第二次降息。總裁John Mushayavanhu以通膨預期穩定及支持成長為理由，儘管油價成本已使通膨由2.9%加速至3.7%。他預期年底通膨低於7%、經濟成長5%，且準備貨幣維持在IMF工作人員監督計畫的目標內。這項決策顯示，同樣的能源衝擊，仍會遇上截然不同的起始利率及國內限制。

## 後續市場觀察重點

達拉斯製造業表現遠強於預期後，美國9月29日將公布8月JOLTS職缺及9月消費者信心；9月30日接續公布ADP就業、8月所得、支出及PCE通膨，以及第2季GDP終值。彭博報導中的經濟學家預期，核心PCE月增0.3%，但統計調整可能使年增率降低最多0.3個百分點。區分修正效果與最新月度動能，對評估Cook所稱短期通膨壓力正在擴大的看法相當重要。10月1日的ISM製造業指數及初領失業救濟金人數，將接續引向10月2日非農就業報告；彭博上週五調查預期新增約9萬個職位、失業率4.1%。

澳洲9月29日決策預期將現金利率上調25個基點至4.6%，雪梨時間下午2時30分公布後一小時，總裁Michele Bullock將召開記者會。真正重要的分歧在於，這次升息後，負債家庭還能承受多少緊縮。日本週三2年期公債標售與週四短觀調查，則在2年期殖利率逼近2%之際，分別檢驗需求與景氣。本週歐元區通膨公布時，ECB總裁的重點已是市場利率帶來的緊縮，而不只是能源最新漲跌。

Paramount計畫週三定價，將把初步認購意向轉為不同順位、幣別及期限的借款條件。由於投資人騰挪資金時，次級信用市場已經重新定價，交易接受度的影響將超出發行人本身。市政債市場尚待觀察，延後的借新還舊交易能否在仍有經濟效益的價格重返市場，或持續壓低發行量。無論初步訂單多大，或發行人是否有能力等待，都不保證次級價格穩定。

能源方面，沙國管線修復已改善實際供給，但外交協議仍未達成，紅海護航能力也不足。油價週一僅吐回部分漲幅後，維持輸送量是眼前的檢驗重點。台北時間週二上午7時15分之前的亞洲早盤，紐西蘭公債開低，澳洲期貨也指向下跌，將美國利率調整延續到下一個交易時段。這些後續交易發生在週一美國公債跌勢完成之後，而不是解釋該日跌勢的原因。

overall_summary.headline: 能源衝擊未解，聯準會升息預期延續，美國公債再度下跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
荷莫茲海峽協議未能推進，能源價格居高不下，美國短天期公債吐回上週五的反彈。盤末報導顯示，10年期殖利率上升9個基點至5.25%，盤中曾觸及5.27%的19年高點。沙烏地阿拉伯管線輸油雖已恢復，布蘭特原油仍收在每桶$105.28。每日殖利率序列中，10年期實質殖利率上升7個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅增加0.4個基點，顯示實質借貸成本上升主導名目殖利率變動。聯準會理事Lisa Cook表示，AI投資已在爭奪電力及營建人力，生產力提升帶來的通膨降溫則要更晚才會出現。

美國投資級、高收益及新興市場硬通貨債券利差明顯擴大。Paramount規模約等值$124億的非投資級債券吸引逾$230億初步訂單，10年期美元券洽談殖利率約9%，仍待最終定價。融資成本升高，使市政債發行人及印度國營企業延後或縮減發行。拉加德強調市場殖利率上升已帶來的抑制效果，協助緩和ECB立即升息的預期。
overall_summary.summary: 沙國恢復管線輸油，使油價漲幅收斂，卻未扭轉借款成本上升；Paramount以高成本籌措收購融資，其他借款人則延後發債。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries resumed their decline on September 28, reversing Friday's relief at shorter maturities as the failure to advance a Hormuz agreement kept energy prices high and investors anticipated further Federal Reserve tightening. The 10-year yield rose 9 basis points to 5.25% in Bloomberg's late-session account, after touching a 19-year high of 5.27%. Brent finished the fixed-income session at $105.28 a barrel, up 0.92%, despite recovering Saudi pipeline shipments that moderated the earlier oil surge.

The pressure was spreading from benchmark rates into the terms on which borrowers could raise money. U.S. investment-grade, high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably. Paramount attracted substantial preliminary demand for its acquisition financing by offering junk-bond yields as high as about 9%, while municipal borrowers and Indian state companies postponed or reduced sales. Fed Governor Lisa Cook added a fresh reason to doubt near-term inflation relief from artificial intelligence: investment was already competing for power and construction workers, while the productivity benefits would arrive later. Across the Atlantic, Christine Lagarde placed more weight on the restraint already being delivered by higher bond yields, tempering expectations for an immediate ECB increase.

## Higher Real Yields Accompany the Renewed Energy Shock

Monday's Treasury selling followed the breakdown in optimism that had helped shorter bonds recover Friday. President Donald Trump had rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen Hormuz, and Tehran maintained its conditions. During the U.S. session, a report that Washington might offer sanctions relief for progress on the nuclear issue helped oil and equities recover from their worst levels. Treasury yields retained most of their rise into late afternoon. Trump subsequently denied offering sanctions relief, leaving the diplomatic route uncertain.

Physical supply provided a more tangible offset. Saudi Arabia resumed exports through its repaired East-West pipeline after damage from drone strikes reportedly launched from Iraq. Flows reached about 3.5 million barrels a day, roughly half the line's capacity. The kingdom had also increased overall exports to more than 5 million barrels a day, a wartime high, using Hormuz as well as its western route, with most shipments heading to Asia. The improvement helped oil pare gains but did not restore normal transit through the strait.

The alternative route remained exposed to Houthi pressure around the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb. EU foreign-policy chief Kaja Kallas said Monday that two countries had indicated possible additional vessels for Operation Aspides. Commercial ships were waiting for escorts that the mission could not provide in sufficient numbers. The operation primarily had three Italian and Greek ships, against an original assessment that at least ten were needed. Kallas proposed using vessels pledged, but not deployed, for a separate prospective Hormuz mission. Additional interest was not yet a completed reinforcement.

By the September 28 observation in Bloomberg's daily yield series, the two-year Treasury yielded 4.932%, up 7.8 basis points, and the five-year 5.071%, up 8.3. The 10-year rose 7.4 basis points to 5.237%, while the 30-year increased 5.4 to 5.548%. The 2s10s spread narrowed only 0.4 basis point to 30.5; 2s30s narrowed 2.4 to 61.6. Short and intermediate maturities therefore participated fully in the renewed decline, unlike Friday's divided performance.

At 10 years, the real yield increased 7 basis points to 2.894%, while the breakeven rose just 0.4 basis point to 2.343%. The day's nominal increase was overwhelmingly an increase in real borrowing costs rather than a comparable jump in long-term inflation compensation. That distinction fits a market expecting the Fed to respond to persistent price pressure. It also explains why another expensive-oil session could be particularly difficult for assets that offer no income: gold futures fell 3.54% to $4,168.40 an ounce, while the Dollar Index gained 0.23% to 101.20.

Cook's Monday remarks addressed the timing mismatch at the heart of the AI inflation debate. She expected productivity gains to deliver modest disinflation over the next few years, but not soon enough to offset broader inflation pressure later in 2026. Data-center investment was already increasing competition for energy and construction labor, she said, against a roughly 5% rise in electricity and water costs over the preceding year. Companies had spent only a fraction of $2 trillion in pledged capital, while AI-related equity gains were also supporting consumption.

The governor supported September's rate increase as necessary to address elevated inflation and said subsequent decisions would depend on economic data. She judged the labor market roughly balanced and gradually improving, with declining unemployment and a resilient broader economy leaving it able to withstand higher rates. Her qualification concerned uncertainty about how quickly AI would lift economy-wide productivity, not a rejection of its eventual benefits. Federal funds futures reflected roughly a 70% chance of another increase in October during Monday's reporting, and swaps fully priced at least three quarter-point increases over the following year, with potential for a fourth.

The day's Dallas Fed manufacturing index supplied a distinct, less dramatic activity observation. September's reading was 9.8, down from 11.6 but well above the forecast of 1. Manufacturing therefore slowed on this measure without approaching the weakness economists had anticipated. The result did not reproduce the acceleration in last week's national business surveys, but it also offered little support for an abrupt collapse in factory activity.

The prospect of eventual demand damage divided bond investors. Wellington's Brij Khurana argued that commodities remaining expensive for so long would erode real incomes and destroy demand, a risk obscured by trading each diplomatic headline. Columbia Threadneedle's Ed Al-Hussainy expected the 2s10s and 5s30s curves to invert within six months as tightening cooled activity. TD Securities' Gennadiy Goldberg took the opposite near-term view: substantial increases were already priced, making further front-end underperformance harder and a steeper curve more likely. Monday's still-positive 2s10s spread did not settle that disagreement.

Jim Bianco, meanwhile, turned constructive on Treasuries for the first time in six years. He increased duration in the index underlying his WisdomTree fund to more than six years, against 5.7 for the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate, while describing the change as gradual rather than an aggressive wager. Bloomberg's return calculations put the 10-year yield near 6% as the level needed over a year to exhaust the income cushion at current prices; a percentage-point yield rise implied a loss of less than 2%, compared with about a 13% gain for an equal decline. These were prospective return scenarios, not protection from another near-term selloff. Bianco viewed yields around current levels as historically normal rather than evidence of imminent distress.

Hedging demand continued to grow alongside those valuation arguments. The 20-day average of options volume on the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF reached a record. Open interest had more than doubled over a year and was approaching the 13.55 million-contract peak reached before the preceding week's expiration. Implied volatility and the premium for bearish puts rose to their highest since late March. Nomura's Alex Kosoglyadov said traditional equity investors were increasingly using rate products as well as equity volatility instruments. The S&P 500 lost 0.77% Monday and the Nasdaq 100 1.08%, bringing the financing-cost adjustment more visibly into stocks.

A New York Fed study published Monday supplied longer-run context for the financing behind Treasury markets. Gara Afonso, Jin-Wook Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas and Ryan Riordan described a roughly $13.5 trillion U.S. repo market, equivalent to 40% of GDP, with about 70% backed by Treasuries. Hedge-fund borrowing rose from $400 billion in 2013 to $1.5 trillion in 2023 and $3 trillion in late 2025; money-market-fund lending reached $3 trillion in January 2026, against $1 trillion five years earlier. Hedge funds also lent about $1.3 trillion in late 2025, including for liquidity management and collateral transformation. The historical expansion shows the scale of financing supporting securities positions; it is not a measurement of Monday's cash flows.

## Paramount Tests Demand as Other Issuers Wait

Paramount Skydance's acquisition financing moved from a prospective supply burden to visible indications of investor appetite, although final pricing remained ahead. Its roughly $12.4 billion-equivalent junk-bond offering had attracted more than $23 billion in orders by Monday morning. Investors had also indicated more than $51 billion of interest in about $32 billion of higher-rated bonds that had not yet launched. Together, the bond offerings form most of the $52 billion package financing the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, alongside $7.5 billion in loans.

The compensation was substantial. A 10-year dollar second-lien note was being discussed around 9%, against a 6.9% average for similarly rated outstanding bonds in a Bloomberg index. A five-year euro junk tranche was offered around 7.5%. The higher-rated portion was planned as eight dollar first-lien tranches with maturities from two to 40 years. The second-lien component comprised five- and eight-year euro notes and five-, eight- and 10-year dollar notes. Preliminary indications could still change once investors saw final terms.

The rating split exposed the assumptions supporting the senior financing. Fitch and S&P assigned investment-grade ratings to the first-lien debt, while Moody's placed it one notch below investment grade; all three rated the second-lien securities as junk. Moody's said the acquisition would add more than $30 billion of debt and leave leverage near seven times earnings. It cited concentrated ownership, plans to place new claims ahead of existing unsecured creditors, and management's mixed record on financial targets. S&P's BBB- assessment instead placed weight on the Ellison family's commitment to reduce leverage to 3.75 times by 2028 and three times in 2029.

The cost of delay falls on Paramount rather than its underwriting banks under the financing structure. The company aimed to price the bonds and loans by Wednesday, and failure to close the $110 billion acquisition before October would require payments of $7 million a day to Warner shareholders. The combination of a large order book and expensive marketed yields thus reflected both investor capacity and the borrower's limited freedom to wait.

Goldman's Amanda Lynam said Monday that heavy high-yield supply was beginning to strain investors' ability to absorb deals, following similar episodes in investment grade earlier in the summer. September junk issuance had reached $38.51 billion by Friday, the busiest month of 2026. She put AI-related borrowing across debt markets near $600 billion this year, with only about 40% attributable to hyperscalers. The financing wave was broad enough that avoiding a few familiar technology names did not eliminate exposure to it.

Individual secondary bonds repriced as banks discussed Paramount's sale. SpaceX's 5.65% notes due in 2033 widened about 36 basis points to 177 over the benchmark, while Oracle's 2.95% 2030 bonds widened about 15 to 160, according to reported Trace observations. Allspring trader Mark Clegg argued that the size of the Paramount offering was forcing investors to reassess spread compensation across the market. A successful placement could also encourage borrowers waiting for a more stable reception.

New reporting on SoftBank's completed offering explained how it had gained access to U.S. institutional capital. The legal work centered on avoiding classification as an investment company under the Investment Company Act, which could have complicated a foreign issuer's access. SoftBank described investment securities as less than 40% of its unconsolidated assets and treated its 86% Arm holding as an operating subsidiary rather than a passive investment. That structure helped enable its Rule 144A offering. The fresh detail concerned access to the investor base, rather than another increase in the already completed financing.

Elsewhere, issuers were choosing to wait. The $1.8 billion Los Angeles Convention Center sale moved to day-to-day status, as did an approximately $777 million Nashville convention-center transaction originally due September 24. A roughly $1.7 billion New Jersey Transportation Trust Fund Authority sale was also put on hold. Benchmark 30-year municipal yields reached 5.18% at 2 p.m. New York time Monday, the highest since at least January 2011 and roughly 60 basis points higher over the month. The increase directly reduced the savings available from refunding older obligations. JPMorgan strategists expected weekly issuance to fall $1 billion-$3 billion below headline supply forecasts if conditions persisted.

Indian borrowers encountered a similar price constraint alongside domestic liquidity withdrawal. Sagarmala Finance canceled a planned blue bond of up to INR6 billion Monday after bids exceeded its expectation of a coupon below 8% on 10-year debt. Power Grid accepted only INR20 billion against a planned INR50 billion, despite receiving offers for the full amount at 7.74%. SIDBI had canceled an INR60 billion December 2029 offering Friday after bids of 7.6%-8.1%, following an earlier September sale of October 2029 debt at 7.70%. Banking-system surplus liquidity had fallen to INR4.6 trillion from nearly INR11 trillion earlier in the month as the RBI drained funds, adding a domestic tightening force to the global yield increase.

PureGym offered a contrasting refinancing case. The budget gym chain marketed £1.4 billion of six-year senior secured debt, with euro notes around 6.5% and sterling around 8%, against yields above 8% on the securities sold in 2023. Fitch upgraded the issuer to B from B-, citing improved performance, new openings and a stronger U.S. business. Proceeds would refinance existing bonds and partially repay preferred financing, although leverage would temporarily rise. An expansion of almost 300 gyms through 2029 was expected to keep free cash flow negative, limiting the benefit of better operating earnings.

Brazilian meatpacker MBRF also began investor calls for a possible first bond offering since Marfrig acquired BRF. The options included long seven-year notes not callable for three years or long 10-year debt not callable for five. S&P and Fitch assigned prospective BB+ ratings. A separate offer to repurchase $467.5 million of 2029 notes expires October 2. No final size or yield for the new financing had been announced.

## Central Banks Weigh the Restraint Already in Markets

Christine Lagarde explicitly identified the global yield increase as a force that would slow euro-area growth and reduce the transmission of energy costs into prices more than the ECB had projected in September. Speaking to European lawmakers Monday, she favored a measured response while second-round effects remained absent. Traders pared tightening expectations, leaving the probability of an October increase below 40%.

Her argument did not dismiss persistent inflation risk. The ECB must anticipate second-round effects rather than wait until they are established, she said, but it was not yet seeing evidence that they were likely to emerge. She described current rates as at the upper end of a neutral range of 2%-2.5%, while stressing that policy was not mechanically set by that estimate. Lagarde also criticized energy-support programs that were broad or open-ended rather than temporary and targeted. Such fiscal measures can sustain spending precisely when higher market rates are beginning to restrain it.

Bank of England Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden added his own conditional support for tightening Monday. He would consider an increase if upside inflation pressures continued building, focusing on second-round effects in domestic food prices and employers' forthcoming wage-settlement plans. He nevertheless judged policy already restrictive. Without the war, he would have expected at least two cuts by now; holding rates since March had therefore delivered additional restraint relative to his earlier outlook. External member Swati Dhingra separately warned that higher rates could weaken investment and the economy's supply capacity. Ramsden's shift broadened the discussion beyond the officials who had spoken last week without eliminating disagreement about the cost of acting.

UK fiscal policy was confronting the same rise in financing costs. Chancellor John Healey pledged Monday that he and Prime Minister Andy Burnham would meet the fiscal rules, pairing an industrial-growth program with spending discipline ahead of the October 28 budget. He committed £6 billion to shipyards, including nuclear deterrence, while announcing a local apprenticeship program and signaling pressure to contain welfare spending. Two-year gilt yields rose as much as 9 basis points to 4.93% before partially retracing as energy prices eased.

The government's room against its principal budget rule was estimated to have roughly halved from the £23.6 billion inherited in the spring. CG Asset Management's Emma Moriarty argued that investors would distinguish sharply between rebuilding headroom toward £20 billion and leaving it near £10 billion. The new first-time-buyer equity-loan program meanwhile sent major homebuilders' shares more than 10% higher. It added an immediate sectoral stimulus while the chancellor was preparing a budget expected to raise taxes and reduce spending elsewhere.

After the U.S. close, the Common Wealth think tank proposed changing the accounting treatment of public corporations so bodies such as GB Energy and the National Wealth Fund could issue debt backed by project revenues outside national fiscal aggregates. It estimated that comparable treatment reduced recorded debt-to-GDP by 2.8 percentage points in France and 10.7 in Germany. The proposal would change who raises investment finance and how it is counted; it was not an adopted relaxation of Britain's rules.

Japan's adjustment was concentrated in expected short rates. The two-year government yield rose as much as 4 basis points to 1.975%, its highest since 1995, and the five-year added 3 to 2.43%. Monday's overnight swaps implied about a 40% chance of an October BOJ increase and fully priced another quarter-point by December. Former BOJ executive director Kazuo Momma argued that a second consecutive monthly increase was possible and that the terminal rate would likely reach about 2% in June or July 2027, above the surveyed economists' 1.75% median. He judged that the recent dissents need not derail normalization, particularly when obstructing it could renew yen weakness and imported inflation.

South Korea's three-year yield jumped 11 basis points to 4.11%, the highest since November 2022, as trading resumed after Thursday-Friday holidays. NH Investment & Securities' Kang Seungwon said another Fed increase in October would most likely cement a Korean move in November. The BOK held a market-review meeting Monday and pledged close monitoring as volatility could expand. The reopening compounded external rates pressure with local concern that strong semiconductor-led growth and imported energy inflation would require more restraint.

Pimco disputed how far Australian tightening could go. Adam Bowe, its Australian portfolio-management head, said Monday that rate increases were fully priced and highlighted opportunities in five- to 10-year debt. Swaps assigned a three-in-four chance to two additional increases next year, taking the policy rate above 5%, but Bowe pointed to households' near-record tax and mortgage burdens relative to income. Data-center investment might support activity for a couple of years while indebted consumers remained much less able to absorb that rate path.

Thailand received an unusually hawkish forecast from JPMorgan's Charnon Boonnuch. He expected three quarter-point increases beginning in Q1 2027, taking the policy rate from 1% to 1.75%, against a consensus for no change through next year. JPMorgan kept growth at 2.5% in both 2026 and 2027, above the central bank's 2.3% and 1.8%, and raised its 2027 inflation forecast by a percentage point to 2.5%. It expected inflation near 4% in Q1. Weak small-business lending and below-potential activity nevertheless kept the bank's forecast at no change for the rest of 2026.

China remained a different duration story. Citi's Wenhan Chen and Rohit Garg expected weak domestic demand and credit creation to support long government bonds, with a 30-year yield target of 1.80% from an entry level of 2.088%. About 90% of the planned CNY1.3 trillion ultra-long special Treasury issuance had already been completed, leaving the remainder likely to finish in October. They also expected CNY360 billion of financial-institution recapitalization to support long-tenor demand. Industrial profits had risen only 4.2% in August from a year earlier, their weakest growth since November's decline, underscoring the limited breadth of the recovery.

The newly detailed U.S.-China tariff arrangement offered a separate, bounded reduction in trade friction: about $30 billion of imports in each direction, against $415 billion in total bilateral goods trade last year. The U.S. list contained 77 entries, while China's covered 1,619 potential imports. Beijing also committed to at least 10 million metric tons of U.S. coal in each of 2027 and 2028. The relief was concentrated in non-sensitive goods while export controls and Taiwan remained unresolved.

## Credit Losses Turn on Cash Flow and Creditor Rank

Merlin Entertainments showed why refinancing a maturity does not necessarily improve existing creditors' position. Its €700 million June 2030 bond traded around 69.3 cents Monday, approximately 12 cents below its level before a £657 million financing announced September 10. The new loans would replace $830 million of unsecured bonds due next year but rank alongside £3.2 billion of other debt, with additional priority claims on valuable UK attractions including the London Eye.

Replacing unsecured claims with secured financing removed part of the loss-absorbing layer beneath existing senior creditors. S&P put the secured debt's B- rating on CreditWatch Negative; Moody's downgraded the loans to Caa2. Merlin had consumed £25 million of cash in the first half. An asset sale should lift liquidity cover above one and a half times the following year's needs, according to S&P, but $2.5 billion of term loans mature in 2029. Polen Capital's Ben Pakenham argued that a substantial earnings recovery or equity injection was needed to restore par value, rather than maturity relief alone.

U.S. leisure borrowers were also showing pressure beneath resilient aggregate consumption. Moody's changed Dave & Buster's outlook to negative Monday after weak earnings. Its 2031 loan was indicated at 61.8 cents, down more than 15 cents since the month's start. Lucky Strike's 2032 loan stood around 79 cents, down 5 over a month, following S&P's downgrade to B- from B on softer performance and acquisition-related leverage. Management attributed its same-store revenue decline to televised sports drawing customers away.

There were meaningful exceptions. AMC completed about $4 billion of financing after its strongest quarter since the pandemic. Michaels received an S&P upgrade to B from B- Monday following better sales and debt reduction; its first- and second-lien ratings rose to B and CCC+, respectively. Both notes traded near 98 cents, about a cent below the preceding week despite the upgrade. S&P still identified a risk of renewed leverage under Apollo ownership, weaker consumer spending, and dependence on Chinese imports and shipping exposed to tariffs and fuel costs.

Australia's Metrics Credit Partners disclosed valuation reductions totaling about A$169 million across three listed funds and halted their trading ahead of a September 30 accounting deadline. The Real Estate Multi-Strategy Fund was reduced by about A$47 million to A$337 million, Income Opportunities Trust by A$73 million to A$643 million, and Master Income Trust by A$49 million to A$2.4 billion. The manager oversees roughly A$40 billion. ASIC had been examining valuation and governance concerns as part of wider private-credit scrutiny, but had not alleged wrongdoing by Metrics. The markdowns were concrete changes in carrying values amid that oversight, not merely another expression of concern about the industry.

Optimum creditors escalated a restructuring dispute into litigation in New York Monday. They sought reversal of transactions they alleged transferred collateral and value to controlling shareholder Patrick Drahi and other insiders. A central complaint concerned preferred shares issued in May through an unrestricted subsidiary: creditors alleged the structure increased the preferred holders' payout if lenders enforced their rights, penalizing enforcement relative to a negotiated deal. Optimum denied wrongdoing and said its actions complied with debt agreements and law. Talks over more than $26 billion of debt were continuing, including with creditors participating in the lawsuit.

OTP Bank's review of a possible Russian exit introduced another balance-sheet trade-off. Chief Executive Peter Csanyi said the review should conclude by year-end as the lender pursued its Baltic expansion through Luminor. OTP said Russian exit rules allowed sellers to realize only about 5% of an asset's market value, making a sale virtually impossible at present. It had repatriated about $880 million in dividends, but said that money was not financing Luminor. Estonia's regulator called the Russian business a key issue in its acquisition review. Bloomberg's documents did not establish sanctions wrongdoing, and OTP said its own review found no non-compliance. Its shares nevertheless fell as much as 3.8% Monday.

## Emerging Debt Meets Country-Specific Setbacks

Emerging-market dollar debt lost its remaining gains for 2026 as higher Treasury yields and wider spreads combined. The Bloomberg EM Hard Currency Aggregate was down about 2.1% in September, while the more duration-sensitive sovereign total-return gauge had fallen about 2.4%. BlackRock's $13 billion EMB fund suffered $610 million of withdrawals in the preceding week, its largest weekly outflow since March. On Monday, EMB's distribution-adjusted return was minus 0.91%.

Managers were responding through both credit quality and interest-rate exposure. Aegon's Jeff Grills had reduced Colombia while adding Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and the Philippines. Neuberger Berman's Gorky Urquieta trimmed Ecuador, the Dominican Republic and Zambia. JPMorgan Asset Management's Pierre-Yves Bareau reduced sensitivity to a credit selloff while shifting some risk toward local markets, including Mexico, where he judged swap pricing too hawkish. These adjustments came with hard-currency spreads near long-run lows, leaving limited compensation for country shocks even before refinancing needs increased.

Ecuador supplied such a shock Monday. President Daniel Noboa unexpectedly replaced Finance Minister Sariha Moya with Bernardo Cordovez, previously chairman of the state social-security institution, an important domestic-bond investor. The 2039 dollar bond fell 2.3 cents to 92.9. The change came despite Noboa saying the preceding week that Moya would meet investors in New York. StoneX's Ramiro Blazquez said the unexplained replacement was unsettling alongside fiscal uncertainty and El Niño.

Cordovez inherits rising fuel-subsidy costs, declining local oil production and refining capacity insufficient for demand. Flooding threatens coastal infrastructure and shrimp and banana exports, while drought in the highlands could disrupt hydroelectric supply. November local elections further complicate spending restraint. Barclays' Jason Keene had downgraded his recommendation the preceding week on subsidies and weather risks; Ecuador's bonds had lost 4.5% during September. The leadership change added uncertainty to those existing pressures rather than resolving them.

Colombia's peso fell 1.5% after President Abelardo de la Espriella said late Sunday that he had instructed his economic team to open IMF talks amid a fiscal crisis. Mexico's peso declined 1.7% toward 18 per dollar, its weakest since late March. Wells Fargo's Alvaro Vivanco attributed the Mexican move partly to an adjustment in popular long-peso and rates-receiver positions. Currency depreciation was becoming another route through which the U.S. repricing could affect local inflation and policy choices.

In Chile, a Bloomberg survey found eleven of nineteen analysts and traders expected the Fed to dominate October market direction. Peso bonds due in 2030 yielded 5.74%, more than 25 basis points higher over September, despite July activity having contracted 1.7% from June. One-year inflation breakevens had risen 56 basis points during the month to 3.87%, and two-year measures about 37 to 3.49%. Markets brought a prospective quarter-point Chilean increase forward to within six months, from at least a year earlier in September. All but one survey respondent nevertheless expected October's meeting to hold at 4.5%. The split reflects immediate currency and energy pressure against a weaker domestic activity backdrop.

Indonesia delivered a favorable resolution for a specific guaranteed credit. The government and PT Penjaminan Infrastruktur Indonesia fully paid the IDR722 billion principal claim after Waskita Karya's missed repayment, with IDR610 billion provided by the government and IDR112 billion by PII. Distribution to bondholders was scheduled for Monday. It was the first payout under the pandemic-era guarantee program and resolved the near-term claim much sooner than its 20-business-day limit. Officials stressed that the payment neither supplied new financing to Waskita nor extinguished the builder's obligation.

Zimbabwe moved against the broader tightening direction, cutting its benchmark from 30% to 27.5% Monday for a second consecutive reduction. Governor John Mushayavanhu cited anchored expectations and support for growth, although inflation had accelerated to 3.7% from 2.9% on oil costs. He expected inflation below 7% at year-end and 5% economic growth, with reserve money within targets under the IMF staff-monitored program. The decision illustrated that the common energy shock was still meeting very different starting rates and domestic constraints.

## Forward Market Significance

The September 29 U.S. calendar brings August JOLTS and September consumer confidence after Dallas manufacturing remained much stronger than expected. September 30 then combines ADP employment with August income, spending and PCE inflation and final Q2 GDP. Economists in Bloomberg's account expect monthly core PCE of 0.3%, while statistical changes may lower the annual measure by as much as 0.3 percentage point. The distinction between revisions and new monthly momentum will matter for Cook's contention that near-term inflation pressure is broadening. October 1 manufacturing ISM and jobless claims lead into October 2 payrolls, with Bloomberg's Friday survey expecting about 90,000 jobs and 4.1% unemployment.

Australia's September 29 decision is expected to raise the cash rate a quarter-point to 4.6%, with Michele Bullock's press conference an hour after the 2:30 p.m. Sydney announcement. The consequential disagreement is how much more tightening indebted households can bear after that move. Japan's Wednesday two-year auction and Thursday Tankan survey provide separate tests of demand and activity as the two-year yield approaches 2%. Euro-area inflation this week will meet an ECB president now emphasizing the tightening already delivered by market rates, not simply the latest movement in energy.

Paramount's planned Wednesday pricing will turn preliminary interest into borrowing terms across seniority, currencies and maturities. Its reception matters beyond the issuer because secondary credit has already repriced as investors make room. In municipal debt, the unresolved question is whether postponed refundings return at economically useful levels or continue to shrink issuance. Neither a large prospective order book nor an issuer's ability to wait guarantees stability in secondary prices.

For energy, Saudi pipeline restoration has improved actual supply while the diplomatic agreement remains elusive and Red Sea escorts remain insufficient. Sustaining those flows is the immediate test after oil gave back part, but not all, of Monday's rise. In early Tuesday Asian trading before 7:15 a.m. Taipei, New Zealand government bonds opened lower and Australian futures pointed to losses, carrying the U.S. rates adjustment into the next session. That later trading followed, rather than explained, Monday's completed Treasury decline.

Split first-lien ratings reflected different leverage assumptions, while the sale pressured secondary spreads. Municipal refundings were postponed and Indian borrowers rejected costly bids. PureGym's improved operations offered a contrasting refinancing case, although expansion would keep free cash flow negative.

section_summaries.section_title: Central Banks Weigh the Restraint Already in Markets
section_summaries.summary: Lagarde favored a measured response as higher yields restrained growth and second-round inflation effects remained absent. Ramsden conditionally supported a BOE increase despite already restrictive policy. Japan and Korea faced renewed short-rate pressure, while Pimco questioned how much Australian households could bear. China remained distinct: weak demand and credit creation supported the case for long bonds.

section_summaries.summary: Merlin's refinancing eased maturities while weakening existing creditors' protection through new secured claims. Dave & Buster's and Lucky Strike showed leisure-sector strain, contrasting with improvement at AMC and Michaels. Metrics marked down three funds by about A$169 million. Optimum creditors sued over alleged collateral transfers, which the company defended; OTP's possible Russian exit faced punitive sale terms.

section_summaries.market_read: Currency depreciation adds another channel through which U.S. repricing can affect local inflation and policy choices.
section_summaries.summary: Higher Treasury yields and wider spreads erased emerging-market dollar debt's remaining 2026 gains. Ecuador's unexpected finance-minister replacement compounded fiscal and weather risks, while Colombia and Mexico faced currency declines. Chile brought prospective tightening forward despite weak activity. Indonesia fully paid Waskita's guaranteed principal claim, and Zimbabwe cut rates despite higher oil-driven inflation.

U.S. inflation and labor releases will test the case for further Fed tightening, with PCE revisions requiring separation from monthly momentum. Paramount's Wednesday pricing will reveal whether preliminary demand translates into durable borrowing terms. Sustained Saudi pipeline flows remain the immediate energy test while Hormuz diplomacy and Red Sea escort capacity remain unresolved.
